assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Split into two genus ranges. In the low-genus range g < m-1, use the multiplicity obstruction to show A_{m,g} is empty, hence N(m,g)=0 and the inequality is immediate. In the range g >= m-1, define a canonical child map by deleting the least effective generator of each numerical semigroup S in A_{m,g}. The existence of an effective generator makes this map well-defined, and deleting such a generator preserves multiplicity while increasing genus by exactly one. Parent recovery from the child's Frobenius number yields injectivity of this map. Finally, an injection A_{m,g} -> A_{m,g+1} implies N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1). Combining the two ranges proves the theorem for all g >= 0.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. If S is a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, then the integers 1,2,...,m-1 are not in S. Consequently g(S) >= m-1. Equivalently, for every integer g with 0 <= g < m-1, there exists no numerical semigroup S with multiplicity m and genus g, so A_{m,g} is empty and N(m,g)=0.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2, and let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m. Suppose g(S) >= m-1. Then S has at least one effective generator; that is, there exists x in S such that x is a minimal generator of S and x > F(S), where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, and let x be an effective generator of S, meaning that x is a minimal generator of S and x > F(S). Define T = S \ {x}. Then T is a numerical semigroup, m(T)=m, g(T)=g(S)+1, and F(T)=x.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Provides the inverse construction needed for uniqueness and injectivity of the child map.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. Let T be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, and let y = F(T) be its Frobenius number. Define P = T ∪ {y}. Then P is a numerical semigroup, m(P)=m, g(P)=g(T)-1, and y is an effective generator of P.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Turns equality of children into equality of parents, which is the core of injectivity.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, let x be an effective generator of S, and define T = S \ {x}. Then S = T ∪ {F(T)}. Equivalently, the parent numerical semigroup S is uniquely recoverable from the child numerical semigroup T by adjoining the Frobenius number of T.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Packages the existence and deletion lemmas into a single function from A_{m,g} to A_{m,g+1}.

Then C(S) is well-defined, C(S) is a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, and g(C(S)) = g(S)+1.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m and g be integers with m >= 2 and g >= m-1. If there exists an injective function from A_{m,g} to A_{m,g+1}, where A_{m,h} denotes the set of numerical semigroups S with multiplicity m(S)=m and genus g(S)=h, then N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1), where N(m,h)=|A_{m,h}|.

shared_context.content: A numerical semigroup is a subset S of N0 = {0,1,2,...} such that 0 is in S, S is closed under addition, and N0 \ S is finite. The multiplicity m(S) is the least positive element of S. The genus g(S) is the cardinality of N0 \ S. If S is not equal to N0, its Frobenius number F(S) is the largest integer not in S. An element x in S \ {0} is a minimal generator of S if there do not exist a,b in S \ {0} with x = a + b. An effective generator of S is a minimal generator x satisfying x > F(S). For integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, let A_{m,g} = {S : S is a numerical semigroup, m(S)=m, g(S)=g}, and let N(m,g) = |A_{m,g}|.
shared_context.label: basic_definitions

previous_attempt_summaries.vet_summary: The decomposition is fatally flawed because several core lemmas are false. In particular, L2 fails for S = <4,5>, which has multiplicity 4 and genus 6 >= 3 but no effective generator at all; L3, L6, and L7 fail already for the ordinary semigroup S = {0,4,5,6,7,...}, where deleting the least effective generator 4 changes the multiplicity from 4 to 5; and L4 fails for the same ordinary example when adjoining the Frobenius number. Assuming the lemmas were true, the assembly would nearly prove the theorem, but step A4 overclaims triviality. There are also self-containment issues with undefined notation such as A_{m,g}, N(m,g), and 'effective generator' in several lemma statements.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix arbitrary integers m >= 2 and g >= 0. Translate numerical semigroups of multiplicity m and genus g into Kunz vectors with coordinate sum g using the bijection from L5, and similarly translate genus g+1 semigroups into Kunz vectors with coordinate sum g+1. Invoke the coordinate-layer injection from L6 to obtain an injective map K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}. Since these Kunz layers are finite, apply the finite-cardinality injection principle from L7 to deduce |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}|. Finally replace these cardinalities by N(m,g) and N(m,g+1) using the equalities from L5. Because m and g were arbitrary, the desired inequality holds for all m >= 2 and g >= 0.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Introduces Apéry representatives and the positive integer coordinates used to encode a numerical semigroup of multiplicity m.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup and let m be a positive integer with m = m(S). Then for each residue class r with 1 <= r <= m-1, there exists a unique least element w_r of S congruent to r modulo m, and Ap(S,m) = {0,w_1,...,w_{m-1}}. Moreover each w_r has the form w_r = r + m k_r for a unique positive integer k_r.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Shows that every numerical semigroup of multiplicity m determines an admissible Kunz vector.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m >= 2. For each r in {1,...,m-1}, let w_r be the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and write w_r = r + m k_r with k_r a positive integer. Then the tuple (k_1,...,k_{m-1}) satisfies the Kunz inequalities: for all integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m >= 2. For each r in {1,...,m-1}, let w_r be the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and write w_r = r + m k_r with k_r a positive integer. Then the genus of S is g(S) = k_1 + k_2 + ... + k_{m-1}.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Provides the inverse construction from an admissible Kunz vector to a numerical semigroup.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2, and let k_1,...,k_{m-1} be positive integers satisfying the Kunz inequalities: for all integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}. Define a subset S(k) of N0 by S(k) = {q m + r : q,r are integers, q >= 0, 0 <= r <= m-1, and either r = 0 or q >= k_r}. Then S(k) is a numerical semigroup, its multiplicity is m, and for each r in {1,...,m-1} the least element of S(k) congruent to r modulo m is w_r = r + m k_r.

lemmas.statement_nl: Fix integers m >= 2 and g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples k = (k_1,...,k_{m-1}) of positive integers such that: (i) for all integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}; and (ii) k_1 + ... + k_{m-1} = g. Also define A_{m,g} to be the set of all numerical semigroups S with multiplicity m(S)=m and genus g(S)=g, and define N(m,g)=|A_{m,g}|. Then there exists a bijection between A_{m,g} and K_{m,g}. Consequently N(m,g) = |K_{m,g}|.

payload.theorem_nl: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= 0, the number N(m, g) of numerical semigroups with multiplicity m and genus g satisfies N(m, g) <= N(m, g + 1).

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix arbitrary integers m >= 2 and g >= 0. Use the bijection between numerical semigroups of multiplicity m and genus g and Kunz vectors of length m-1 with coordinate sum g to rewrite N(m,g) as the cardinality of a Kunz layer K_{m,g}. Do the same for genus g+1. Prove that each Kunz layer is finite. Invoke the explicit injection from K_{m,g} into K_{m,g+1}. Apply the general principle that an injection between finite sets yields an inequality of cardinalities. Substitute back the identifications N(m,g)=|K_{m,g}| and N(m,g+1)=|K_{m,g+1}|. Since m and g were arbitrary, conclude the theorem for all m >= 2 and g >= 0.

steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the concluding consequence stated in L5 for the fixed parameters m and g.

steps.derives: For the same fixed integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, if K_{m,g+1} is defined by the same Kunz inequalities with coordinate sum g+1, then N(m,g+1) = |K_{m,g+1}|.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L5 with the genus parameter replaced by g+1. Since g >= 0, the integer g+1 is also in the allowed range.

steps.derives: For the fixed integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, the set K_{m,g} is finite.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of L6.

steps.derives: For the same fixed integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, the set K_{m,g+1} is finite.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L6 with g replaced by g+1.

steps.derives: For the fixed integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, there exists an injective function Phi_{m,g} : K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the assertion of L7.

Step A3 gives finiteness of K_{m,g}. Step A4 gives finiteness of K_{m,g+1}. Step A5 gives an injective function from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}. Therefore the hypotheses of L8 are satisfied with X = K_{m,g}, Y = K_{m,g+1}, and f = Phi_{m,g}, so L8 yields |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}|.
By A1, replace N(m,g) with |K_{m,g}|. By A2, replace N(m,g+1) with |K_{m,g+1}|. Substituting these equalities into the inequality from A6 gives N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1).

lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a subset of N0 = {0,1,2,...} such that 0 belongs to S, S is closed under addition, and N0 \ S is finite; in other words, S is a numerical semigroup. Let m be the least positive element of S, and assume m >= 1. Then for every integer r with 1 <= r <= m-1, there exists a unique least element w_r of S that is congruent to r modulo m. If the Apéry set with respect to m is defined by Ap(S,m) = {s in S : s - m is not in S}, then Ap(S,m) = {0, w_1, ..., w_{m-1}}. Moreover each w_r can be written uniquely in the form w_r = r + m k_r for a positive integer k_r.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a subset of N0 = {0,1,2,...} such that 0 belongs to S, S is closed under addition, and N0 \ S is finite; in other words, S is a numerical semigroup. Let m be the least positive element of S, and assume m >= 2. For each integer r with 1 <= r <= m-1, let w_r be the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and write w_r = r + m k_r with k_r a positive integer. Then the tuple (k_1, ..., k_{m-1}) satisfies the Kunz inequalities: for all integers i and j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a subset of N0 = {0,1,2,...} such that 0 belongs to S, S is closed under addition, and N0 \ S is finite; in other words, S is a numerical semigroup. Let m be the least positive element of S, and assume m >= 2. For each integer r with 1 <= r <= m-1, let w_r be the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and write w_r = r + m k_r with k_r a positive integer. Define the genus of S to be g(S) = |N0 \ S|, the number of nonnegative integers not in S. Then g(S) = k_1 + k_2 + ... + k_{m-1}.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. Let k = (k_1, ..., k_{m-1}) be a tuple of positive integers satisfying the Kunz inequalities: for all integers i and j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}. Define a subset S(k) of N0 = {0,1,2,...} by S(k) = {q m + r : q and r are integers, q >= 0, 0 <= r <= m-1, and either r = 0 or q >= k_r}. Then S(k) is a numerical semigroup, meaning that 0 belongs to S(k), S(k) is closed under addition, and N0 \ S(k) is finite. Its least positive element is m. For each integer r with 1 <= r <= m-1, the least element of S(k) congruent to r modulo m is exactly r + m k_r.

lemmas.statement_nl: Fix integers m and g with m >= 2 and g >= 0. Define A_{m,g} to be the set of all subsets S of N0 = {0,1,2,...} such that: 0 belongs to S, S is closed under addition, N0 \ S is finite, the least positive element of S is m, and |N0 \ S| = g. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples k = (k_1, ..., k_{m-1}) of positive integers such that: for all integers i and j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}, and also k_1 + ... + k_{m-1} = g. Then there exists a bijection between A_{m,g} and K_{m,g}. Consequently, if N(m,g) denotes the cardinality |A_{m,g}|, then N(m,g) = |K_{m,g}|.
